title: Introduce pathwise invocation attributor and decibel alerting
author: Marina Costa
body:
Motivation: long-tail cost and latency noise is currently hard to attribute across multi-stage invocations (routing -> model selection -> token generation). Teams need per-path cost signatures so SRE and product can correlate expensive tails with prompt shapes and routing decisions. This PR adds a lightweight pathwise invocation attributor that synthesizes a stable path-hash, per-stage token counters, and a set of cost-sentinel metrics that make long-tail attribution visible in dashboards and alerts.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds an observation pipeline transform (telemetry/transformers/pathwise_attributor.py) that consumes invocation spans and emits three new metric families (path_hash: gauge with string label, path_token_count: histogram, cost_sentinel: gauge) plus associated span annotations. Exposes path_hash and stage breakdowns to the metrics ingestion layer and wires a new dashboard (observability/dashboards/pathwise_cost_overview.json) with a path cohorting panel and stacked token-cost waterfall. Introduces a new alert type we call "decibel" alerting — a short-window burst detector tuned to surface sudden increases in pathwise cost concentration (example rule added to observability/alerts/decibel_rules.yaml). Adds SDK tagging support for both Python and TypeScript so customers can opt into path attribution at the client level (redwood-sdk-python/redwood/telemetry.py, redwood-sdk-typescript/src/telemetry.ts).

Implementation notes: Path hashing is stable and intentionally low-entropy: we canonicalize the invocation trace to stage names and non-sensitive prompt shape keys (length, token type counts) before hashing. This preserves privacy while ensuring similar invocation shapes map to the same path. The attributor runs as a stateless transform in the telemetry pipeline and enriches traces with a path_hash label and per-stage micro-metrics (token_count_{stage}, cost_estimate_{stage}). We also added a lightweight reservoir sampler in pathwise_attributor so we can generate representative example trace snippets for the dashboard without storing full payloads.

Files touched (high-level): telemetry/transformers/pathwise_attributor.py; telemetry/tests/test_pathwise_attributor.py; observability/dashboards/pathwise_cost_overview.json; observability/alerts/decibel_rules.yaml; redwood-sdk-python/redwood/telemetry.py; redwood-sdk-typescript/src/telemetry.ts; docs/observability/pathwise-attribution.md; observability/runbooks/decibel-alert-runbook.md; infra/monitoring/metrics-mappings.yaml; observability/scripts/seed_sample_traces.py; e2e/observability/pathwise_integration.yaml; charts/observability-values.yaml.

Backward compatibility and migration: The new metrics are additive. Existing dashboards and alerts are unchanged. We added a feature flag (telemetry.feature_flags.enable_path_attrib) defaulting to off; rollout plan below.

Testing and QA: Unit tests cover hash stability and label scrubber (telemetry/tests/test_pathwise_attributor.py). Integration test (e2e/observability/pathwise_integration.yaml) runs a tiny synthetic workload to ensure metrics appear in the collector. Manual validation performed on staging: launched synthetic burst, verified decibel alert fired on path A and a follow-up dashboard panel populated with representative traces. CI flake: one flaky test (observability/test_dashboard_renderer) reran and passed; CI status green on merge.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag gated deploy to staging (telemetry transform) 2) Enable SDK tagging in internal QA apps to generate representative paths 3) Gradual enable for 5% production traffic and monitor decibel alerts for false positives 4) Increase to 25% then 100% over 48 hours if no regressions.

Operational notes: Decibel alerts are intentionally high-sensitivity; they are configured to create 'investigate' level incidents (not paging by default) to avoid churn. We added a suppression window and auto-mitigations for noisy customers in observability/alerts/decibel_rules.yaml. If the path_hash cardinality grows beyond thresholds we fall back to prefix-cohorting by path_prefix (configurable in infra/monitoring/metrics-mappings.yaml).

Checklist:
- [x] Add pathwise attributor transform and tests
- [x] Add dashboard panels and notebook for deep dive
- [x] Add decibel alert rules and runbook
- [x] Add SDK opt-in telemetry hooks
- [x] Add e2e integration and staging verification
- [x] Document feature and migration in docs/observability/pathwise-attribution.md

Related work: builds on ENG-2468 (token cohorting prototype) and borrows reservoir sampling helpers from ENG-1856. Related dashboards: invocation-sankey (PR 262345) and token-cost-atlas.

Rollout/merge decision: reviewed and approved; merging now by squash.

review_comments: Amit Patel: Nice approach. Please confirm privacy review for hash inputs and add a unit test that verifies that literal prompt tokens are not included in the hash.
Sophie Lin: Can we reduce cardinaility exposure by coarsening token-type buckets? Also request to add threshold examples for the decibel alert in the runbook.
Marina Costa (author): Addressed — added scrubber and explicit tests; documented coarsening config and added runbook thresholds; removed raw prompt fields from telemetry payloads.
Amit Patel: Approved after test tweak and minor docs edits.
Sophie Lin: Approved. CI green after rerun.

release_notes: Add pathwise invocation attribution and decibel alerting: new metrics (path_hash, path_token_count, cost_sentinel), dashboard panels, SDK opt-in hooks, and alert runbook. Feature gated; opt-in via telemetry.feature_flags.enable_path_attrib.
notes_for_oncall: If decibel alerts begin firing across >3 distinct path cohorts in a 15m window, mute the rule and open an investigation ticket. Use observability/runbooks/decibel-alert-runbook.md to triage.
